messages: maya: Hey team — customer on acme-prod reporting 403 when uploading debug bundle from the private collector. Root log shows `403 Forbidden` and `x-request-id=rcv-9f1a`. They say bundle creation finished but upload fails. Can SRE generate a fresh signed URL and also collecting repro steps. devon: can you paste the collector logs + the exact curl command you used? also need collector version and bundle md5/size. maya: Collector version: `rw-collector 1.2.3`. Log excerpt: ``` 2026-02-12T18:22:14Z collector: upload start path=/var/tmp/debug-20260212.tar.gz size=24576000 2026-02-12T18:22:24Z http: PUT https://s3-private.example.com/... 403 Forbidden req=rcv-9f1a 2026-02-12T18:22:24Z debug: upload-response body={"error":"AccessDenied","requestId":"rcv-9f1a"} ``` Used the CLI helper `rw-collector upload --output debug.tar.gz` (default presign flow). md5: `abcdef1234567890`, size: `24MB`. samir: 403 + AccessDenied usually means presigned URL expired or wrong headers. TTL for presigns in this cluster is 10m by default. Did the customer wait >10m between creating bundle and uploading? maya: they say upload started within 2 mins. also they attempted a manual curl (from their network) and got same 403. here's their curl attempt (sanitized): ``` curl -v -X PUT "https://s3-private.example.com/abcd?X-Amz-Signature=..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \ --data-binary @debug-20260212.tar.gz ``` devon: can you run the curl locally with `-v` and paste the full response headers + body? also include `--trace-ascii` output if possible. we need the exact response S3 returns. maya: pasted output from customer: ``` * Connected to s3-private.example.com (10.10.10.5) > PUT /abcd?X-Amz-Signature=... HTTP/1.1 > Host: s3-private.example.com > Content-Type: application/gzip < HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden < x-amz-request-id: rcv-9f1a < x-amz-id-2: ... < Content-Type: application/xml AccessDenied Request has expired rcv-9f1a ``` jen: "Request has expired" implies clock skew or signature TTL. please ask them to check `date`/`timedatectl` on the host. NTP drift has bitten customers before. devon: also show them how to reproduce the bundle creation + upload in one go locally (so presign isn't stale). example steps: ``` # generate bundle and upload immediately rw-collector collect --redact --output debug.tar.gz --trace > collector.log 2>&1 rw-collector upload --file debug.tar.gz --verbose # or use curl with the presign printed by upload command ``` maya: note: they did run `--redact` but later found emails inside the tar. logs show `redaction=skipped: missing rules` earlier in the run. suspect private config missing redact rules in the deployment's collector configmap. samir: ok will generate a new presigned URL with TTL 15m and also check the collector config on that customer's private control plane for redact rules. creating URL now — I'll post it here when ready. ops-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-4321 created: https://tickets.internal/INC-2026-4321 :robot_face: samir: new presigned URL (masked): `https://s3-private.example.com/abcd?X-Amz-Signature=NEW...` TTL=15m. maya: please try upload with `-v` and `--max-time 120`. maya: re-ran curl right away using the new URL: ``` curl -v -X PUT "https://s3-private.example.com/abcd?X-Amz-Signature=NEW..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/gzip" \ --data-binary @debug-20260212.tar.gz --max-time 120 ``` Response: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and body empty. upload completed. maya: confirmed customer also retried and upload succeeded. we still need to fix the missing redact rules. attaching collector log excerpt showing config load failure: `error loading config: collectors.redact.rules: not found`. devon: steps for ops to remediate: - add default redact rules to the private control plane configmap (see /ops/templates/collector-redact.yaml) - roll restart collector pod or apply config - validate with `rw-collector collect --redact --output test.tar.gz` and inspect tar for PII maya: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and link INC-2026-4321. :thumbsup: support-bot: Reminder: please add the final resolution and root cause to the ticket.
